source.purpose: Reference database for PSLE Science application answers, experiment-process skills, command words, lab apparatus and scientific reasoning. This source informs training-model generation and AI marking but does not overwrite the existing memorisation bank unless explicitly approved.

answering_principles.rule: For energy-conversion explanations, state the relevant initial energy form, use 'converted to', state the next energy form(s), and link the conversion to the observed motion/result. If comparing two situations, identify where extra energy is dissipated, such as heat due to friction.

For force questions, identify the force, state the direction or interaction when relevant, then explain its effect on motion or shape. Effects include making a stationary object move, speeding up, slowing down, stopping, changing direction or changing shape.

For experimental-process questions, identify aim, hypothesis when required, changed variable, measured variable and variables kept the same. A fair test changes only one variable while all other relevant variables are kept constant.
Reliability is improved by repeating the experiment to obtain consistent/similar results and calculating an average when appropriate. More repeated trials increase reliability.

Accuracy means results are close to the actual value and depends on correct apparatus/procedure/reading. Reliability means repeated results are consistent/similar. Do not confuse accuracy with reliability.
A control set-up uses the same conditions but without the independent variable so that the effect of the changed variable can be compared and confirmed.

Choose apparatus according to what is measured and the required range/precision. For liquid volume, prefer a measuring cylinder to a beaker for more accurate readings; for small precise volumes use a syringe/dropper when suitable.

Before answering, identify the command word and match the response form to it. 'State' requires a concise answer; 'compare' requires similarities and/or differences; 'infer' requires a conclusion based on observations; 'relate' requires explaining a relationship; 'trace' requires following a path.

key_ideas: More mass gives an object more gravitational potential energy at the same height.
Greater height gives an object more gravitational potential energy for the same mass.
Stretching or compressing an elastic object stores elastic potential energy.
When released, elastic potential energy can be converted to kinetic energy.
When an object slows because of friction, some kinetic energy is converted to heat energy and sometimes sound energy.
On a smoother path, less kinetic energy is converted to heat due to friction, so more kinetic energy remains for motion.
When an object rises, kinetic energy can be converted to gravitational potential energy; when it falls, gravitational potential energy can be converted to kinetic energy.
answering_patterns: Initial energy → converted to → final energy → observed result
Comparison: identify which set-up loses more energy as heat/sound due to friction, then link to distance/speed/result.

key_ideas: A force is a push or a pull.
A force can make a stationary object move, speed up, slow down, stop, change direction or change shape.
Four main forces shown: magnetic force, elastic spring force, gravitational force and frictional force.
Gravitational force pulls objects towards the centre of Earth and can act at a distance.
Greater mass gives greater gravitational force; greater distance between objects gives weaker gravitational force.
Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is not a force; weight is a force caused by gravity and can vary with gravitational force.
Frictional force opposes motion and is produced when surfaces are in contact and move/rub against each other.
Rougher surfaces and greater load/mass generally increase frictional force between surfaces.
Lubricants, rollers/wheels and streamlined shapes can reduce friction in suitable contexts.
Elastic spring force acts when an elastic object is stretched or compressed and tends to return it to its original shape.
Greater extension/compression of the same spring gives greater elastic spring force; a stiffer spring gives greater elastic spring force for the same extension/compression.
Magnetic force can be attraction or repulsion and can act at a distance.
Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
A stronger magnet exerts a greater magnetic force.
answering_patterns: D/E: quote the observed movement/change. S/R: identify force and mechanism. L/R: state effect on motion/shape asked.
For friction comparisons: surface/load difference → friction greater/less → object slows/moves more/less → requested outcome.
For elastic force: amount of stretch/compression or stiffness → elastic force strength → return/motion result.

key_ideas: Aim: purpose of the experiment.
Hypothesis: a prediction/relationship involving the changed and measured variables.
Changed/independent variable: what the investigator changes.
Measured/dependent variable: what is measured as the effect.
Variables kept the same: conditions kept constant to ensure a fair test.
Relationship from data should state how the measured variable changes as the changed variable increases/decreases.
Procedural steps should be clear, ordered and include relevant apparatus, quantities and measurements.
Reliability: repeat the experiment and obtain consistent/similar results; calculate an average where appropriate.
Accuracy: use suitable apparatus and follow the method carefully so readings are close to the actual value.
Control set-up: same conditions but without the independent variable.

book_example.aim: Find out how the amount of carbon dioxide affects the number of bubbles produced per minute by a water plant.
book_example.measured_variable: Number of bubbles produced per minute
book_example.relationship_pattern: As the amount of carbon dioxide increases, the number of bubbles produced per minute increases.
book_example.reliability_improvement: Repeat the experiment several times and calculate the average reading.

apparatus.name: Measuring cylinder
apparatus.use: Measure liquid volume with greater precision than a beaker

apparatus.name: Beaker
apparatus.use: Hold and estimate/moderately measure liquid volume

apparatus.name: Retort stand
apparatus.use: Clamp and hold objects in a fixed position

apparatus.name: Funnel
apparatus.use: Pour liquids/solids into containers with small openings without spilling

measurement_rules: Read liquid level at eye level where appropriate.
Use the smallest suitable scale/most precise suitable apparatus for the required measurement.
For volume of an irregular solid, use water displacement: initial water volume → submerge object fully → final volume; object volume = final - initial.
Choose a measuring cylinder rather than a beaker when an accurate liquid-volume measurement is required.

terms.boiling: change from liquid to gas at a fixed temperature known as the boiling point due to heat gain
terms.breathing: taking in and giving out of air through the nose/mouth
terms.condensation: change from gas to liquid due to heat loss
terms.evaporation: change from liquid to gas due to heat gain and can occur at any temperature
terms.fertilisation: fusion of male and female reproductive cells
terms.freezing: change from liquid to solid at a fixed temperature known as the freezing point due to heat loss
terms.gaseous_exchange: taking in oxygen and removing carbon dioxide
terms.germination: process when a seed grows into a seedling
terms.melting: change from solid to liquid at a fixed temperature known as melting point due to heat gain
terms.pollination: transfer of pollen grains from anther of one flower to stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same type/species
terms.respiration: breaking down of glucose/sugar with release of energy in living cells
terms.seed_dispersal: seeds/fruits are scattered away from the parent plant to avoid overcrowding
terms.photosynthesis: green plants take in water and carbon dioxide and trap sunlight with chlorophyll to produce food/sugar/glucose and oxygen

command_words.classify: group things based on common characteristics
command_words.compare: identify similarities and differences between objects, concepts or processes
command_words.construct: put components together based on a given plan
command_words.describe: state in words, using diagrams where appropriate, the main points of a topic
command_words.discuss: reflect on and explore a topic in speech or writing
command_words.differentiate: identify differences between objects, concepts or processes
command_words.identify: select and/or name the object, event, concept or process
command_words.infer: draw a conclusion based on observations
command_words.investigate: find out by carrying out experiments
command_words.list: give a number of points/items without elaboration
command_words.manipulate: control an object in order to explore and discover its behaviour
command_words.measure: obtain a reading from a suitable measuring instrument
command_words.observe: obtain information through the use of the senses
command_words.recognise: identify facts, characteristics or concepts critical to understanding a situation/event/process/phenomenon
command_words.relate: identify and explain a relationship between objects, concepts or processes
command_words.show_an_understanding: recall, translate, explain and apply information
command_words.state: give a concise answer with little or no supporting argument

items: Bird groups: FARM = Fish, Amphibians, Reptiles, Mammals, with Birds/Insects included in the page's grouping aid.
Seed dispersal: WEWA = Wind, Explosive action, Water, Animal.
Photosynthesis needs: carbon dioxide, water, chlorophyll, light; produces oxygen and food/sugar; excess stored as starch.
Materials memory aid: 'We Can Move FAST' for Waterproof, Conductivity, Magnetic/non-magnetic, Flexibility, Ability to sink/float, Strength, Transparency.
Magnetic metals: Iron, Steel, Cobalt, Nickel.
Evaporation factors: WET = Wind, Exposed surface area, Temperature.
Condensation: WC^2CW = source of Water vapour → Contact/touches → Cooler surface/air → Condense → Water droplets.
Electricity/electromagnet: CEE / CEEE prompts for Circuit, Electric current, Effect/Electromagnet, Effects.

integration_guidance.pupil_facing_framework: Keep D/E → S/R → L/R as the only main answering framework shown to the pupil.
ai_marker_use: Use command words to decide whether D/E, S/R and/or L/R are actually required.
Use process-skill rules for fair-test, reliability, accuracy, variables and control-set-up questions.
Use exact scientific vocabulary from the source when generating full training answers.
Do not penalise scientifically equivalent wording if all required concepts and links are present.
Do not silently replace the memorised 89-bank phrasing with book wording.
